title: OECD TALIS Teacher Survey: Collaborative Lesson Study (Jugyokenkyu), Administrative Load, and Self-Efficacy Paradox in Japan
source_name: OECD (Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development) Directorate for Education and Skills
description: International comparative survey of lower secondary educators and school leaders across OECD countries, investigating collaborative lesson study practices (Jugyokenkyu), excessive administrative workloads, instructional self-efficacy, and occupational satisfaction.
observation_unit: Cross-national comparative data across OECD TALIS cycles (2013-2024)
sample_population_note: Representative sample of lower secondary teachers and principals (approx. 260,000 teachers across 48 countries)
title_ja: 【OECD TALIS】授業研究（Jugyokenkyu）と事務過重負担・自己効力感の国際比較多変量分析

research_angles.title: The Jugyokenkyu Paradox: World-Class Collaborative Lesson Study Coexisting with Subdued Teacher Self-Efficacy in Japan
research_questions: Why does Japan rank highest in collaborative peer lesson study yet lowest in instructional self-efficacy?
Does excessive administrative clerical burden suppress teacher job satisfaction regardless of collaborative collegiality?
hypotheses: Clerical burden hours exhibit a strong negative relationship with job satisfaction across countries.
Collaborative lesson study operates as an essential professional development pillar, with clean multicollinearity diagnostics (VIF < 2.0).
research_angles.theoretical_framework: Self-Efficacy Theory (Bandura) and Communities of Practice (Lave & Wenger)
